outcome: Nothing since 26 January 2024 settles the conjecture or a restricted case of it. The in-window items I could identify are a June 2026 ICM survey that reports it open, one August 2026 finite-Morley-rank programme paper whose body I could not read, and neighbouring results on other conjectures (Borovik–Cherlin, generic automorphisms, sharply 2-transitive groups); the landmark restricted cases (rank 3, even and mixed type, odd-type reductions) all predate the window.
problem_asks: Every simple group G whose first-order theory is ℵ0-stable is a simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field (read: G is isomorphic to the group of K-points of a simple algebraic group over some algebraically closed field K). Parts: (a) the hypothesis is ℵ0-stability of Th(G), not finite Morley rank; for a countable language this is the same as ω-stability, which is the wording used by the Wikipedia 'Stable group' article. (b) The frozen wording says 'a simple group' and does not say 'infinite'. Read literally, a finite simple group has a theory with only finite models, which is ℵ0-stable, and it is not an algebraic group over an algebraically closed field, so the literal statement fails at finite simple groups; the intended class is evidently infinite simple groups, which is how the Wikipedia 'Stable group' article states it. (c) The conclusion is a universal claim over all such groups, and its content is that the group is the K-point group of a simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field. The literature (Cherlin, Tent 2026, groupprops) overwhelmingly states and studies the restricted form for simple groups of finite Morley rank; the bullet's ℵ0-stable form is the broader one.

events.what_happened: Borovik, Burdges and Cherlin, 'Involutions in groups of finite Morley rank of degenerate type' (arXiv:0711.4166, posted 27 Nov 2007; Selecta Math. 13 (2007) 1-22). Per the arXiv abstract page as summarised by my fetch (paraphrase, not verbatim): a connected group of finite Morley rank with a finite Sylow 2-subgroup has trivial Sylow 2-subgroup, i.e. a Feit-Thompson-type statement for finite Morley rank. A search excerpt also gives: for an involution a in a connected group of finite Morley rank, the Sylow 2-subgroup of C(a) is infinite (not opened).
events.revisions: Single version (v1) on arXiv; journal reference Selecta Math. 13 (2007) 1-22.
events.delivers: For connected groups of finite Morley rank: a finite Sylow 2-subgroup forces the Sylow 2-subgroup to be trivial, so degenerate type has no involutions. For a simple group of finite Morley rank this removes degenerate type from the possible shapes of a counterexample (the 2026 Tent survey summarises it this way, per a search excerpt). Restricted to finite Morley rank; says nothing about ω-stable groups outside finite Morley rank.
events.remains: Simple groups of finite Morley rank with nontrivial Sylow 2-subgroup (even, mixed and odd types), and every infinite simple ω-stable group outside finite Morley rank.
events.direction: Narrows the possible shape of a counterexample (it excludes degenerate type); does not prove or refute the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Borovik, Burdges and Nesin, 'Uniqueness cases in odd type groups of finite Morley rank' (arXiv:0711.4167, posted 27 Nov 2007). Per the arXiv abstract page (quoted): 'we analyze a proper 2-generated core in a minimal counter example to the Cherlin-Zilber Algebraicity Conjecture for simple groups of finite Morley rank. We ultimately show that such a group is strongly embedded and the ambiant group is minimal connected simple.' The DOI on the page (10.1112/jlms/jdm106) suggests J. London Math. Soc., which the page does not confirm.
events.revisions: Single version (v1) on arXiv.
events.delivers: A reduction for a minimal counterexample: its 2-generated core forces it to be strongly embedded in a minimal connected simple ambient group. This narrows the form a counterexample could take; it does not settle any class of groups.
events.remains: All of the odd-type case beyond this reduction; the result is conditional on the group being a minimal counterexample.
events.doubts: The arXiv page does not confirm the journal. A search excerpt attributes to this group of authors a statement that a tame counterexample has Prüfer rank at most two; the abstract page does not say that, so I have not recorded it as their result.
events.direction: A reduction of the minimal counterexample; neutral on whether a counterexample exists.

events.what_happened: Borovik and Burdges, 'A New Trichotomy Theorem' (arXiv:0711.4169, posted 27 Nov 2007). Per the arXiv abstract page as summarised by my fetch (paraphrase): a minimal counterexample to the Cherlin-Zilber algebraicity conjecture for simple groups of finite Morley rank has normal 2-rank at most two; this is a version of Borovik's trichotomy that does not need tameness assumptions; no groups lie between the generic case (Lie rank at least three) and the quasithin case (Lie rank one or two). A search excerpt of the same paper gives the odd-type K*-group version: such a group either has normal rank at most two, or is an algebraic group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic not 2.
events.revisions: Single version (v1) on arXiv; no journal reference on the page.
events.delivers: Reduces a minimal counterexample to normal 2-rank at most two, or to the algebraic characteristic-not-2 case. Restricted to finite Morley rank; a reduction, not a class of groups settled.
events.remains: The normal 2-rank at most two case, which the excerpt says is still open; the characteristic-2 and other identification steps.
events.direction: Reduces a minimal counterexample to a narrow shape; neutral on existence.

events.what_happened: Burdges, 'Signalizers and balance in groups of finite Morley rank' (arXiv:0711.4210, v1 posted 27 Nov 2007; v2 28 Nov 2008). Per the arXiv abstract as summarised from quoted segments: 'We show that a minimal counter example to the Cherlin-Zilber Algebraicity Conjecture for simple groups of finite Morley rank has Prufer 2-rank at most two.' The paper covers signalizer functor theory and identifies groups of Lie rank at least three, leaving uniqueness cases to earlier articles; PSL2, PSL3, PSp4 and G2 each need their own identification theorem afterwards.
events.revisions: v1 27 Nov 2007; v2 28 Nov 2008. No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Reduction: a minimal counterexample has Prüfer 2-rank at most two. A search excerpt states the K*-group version: a simple K*-group of finite Morley rank and odd type is algebraic or has Prüfer rank at most two. Restricted to finite Morley rank.
events.remains: Odd-type groups of Prüfer 2-rank at most two, including the identification of PSL2, PSL3, PSp4 and G2 configurations; the rest of the conjecture.
events.direction: Reduces a minimal counterexample to Prüfer 2-rank at most two; neutral on existence.

events.what_happened: Burdges and Cherlin, 'A generation theorem for groups of finite Morley rank' (arXiv:0801.3957, v1 25 Jan 2008; v2 7 Nov 2008). Per the arXiv page as summarised: treats two forms of the uniqueness cases in classifying large simple K*-groups of finite Morley rank of odd type (large meaning Prüfer 2-rank at least three); extends earlier results for Prüfer 2-rank at least three to PSp4 and G2; carries out the analysis for L*-groups. (A search result mislabelled these authors as Berkman and Borovik; the arXiv page names Burdges and Cherlin.)
events.delivers: Uniqueness-case steps for odd-type simple K*-groups of finite Morley rank with large 2-rank, and identification cases for PSp4 and G2 in that setting. Does not by itself exclude or produce a counterexample.
events.remains: Odd-type groups of small 2-rank; the identification steps the abstract does not claim to complete; the rest of the conjecture.
events.direction: Advances the odd-type programme for large 2-rank; neutral on existence of a counterexample.

events.what_happened: Borovik, Burdges and Nesin, 'Uniqueness Cases in Odd Type Groups of Finite Morley Rank, Revisited' (arXiv:1111.7187, posted 30 Nov 2011). Per the arXiv page as summarised: versions of the Strong Embedding Theorem and the Uniqueness Subgroup Theorem for odd-type groups of finite Morley rank, stated as needed for permutation actions and modules. The page does not mention the Cherlin-Zilber conjecture.
events.revisions: Single version (v1).
events.delivers: Tool theorems for the odd-type analysis. The abstract page makes no claim about the conjecture itself, so as far as I can tell it bears on the programme rather than on the statement.
events.remains: The whole conjecture.
events.direction: Tool result; no stated direction on the conjecture.

events.remains: Mixed type for groups that are not tame, and all other types for the non-tame case.

events.what_happened: Even type of the algebraicity conjecture, settled across several papers by Altinel, Borovik and Cherlin and consolidated in their monograph 'Simple Groups of Finite Morley Rank' (AMS Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 145, 2008). Per secondary search excerpts (the 2024 Cherlin survey excerpt and the Tent 2026 summary), a simple group of finite Morley rank with an infinite elementary abelian 2-subgroup (even type) is isomorphic to a simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2; one secondary summary dates the weakly-embedded-subgroup theorem to 1999. I did not open any primary paper for this event, so the dates and the exact statement are unverified.
events.revisions: The 1999 date is from a secondary summary, not from a primary source; the monograph is dated 2008.
events.delivers: Even Sylow-2 type: the group is algebraic in characteristic 2 (per the secondary excerpts). Restricted to even type within finite Morley rank.
events.remains: Odd type and degenerate type; the mixed type is treated separately.

events.what_happened: Olivier Frecon, 'Bad groups in the sense of Cherlin' (arXiv:1607.02994, v1 11 Jul 2016; v2 10 Nov 2016). Per the arXiv abstract page (fetched): there is no bad group in the sense of Cherlin; equivalently every simple group of Morley rank 3 is isomorphic to PSL2(K) for an algebraically closed field K. Published as 'Simple groups of Morley rank 3 are algebraic', J. Amer. Math. Soc. 31 (2018), 643-659 (per a search result for the journal page; not opened).
events.delivers: The conjecture holds for simple groups of finite Morley rank 3 (each is PSL2(K) for an algebraically closed field K). Restricted to finite Morley rank exactly 3.
events.remains: Every rank other than 3 for finite Morley rank; every infinite simple ω-stable group outside finite Morley rank.

events.what_happened: Bruno Poizat and Frank Olaf Wagner, 'Comments on a Theorem by Olivier Frecon' (arXiv:1609.06229, in French; v1 20 Sep 2016; v2 29 Sep 2016). In particular, Frecon's Theorem follows: There is no bad group of Morley rank 3.' The page claims no gap or error in Frecon's theorem.
events.delivers: A generalisation of the rank-3 case: no sad group of Morley rank 2n+1 with an abelian Borel subgroup of rank n, with Frecon's theorem as the case n = 1. Same restriction as frecon-rank3-2016: finite Morley rank, rank 3 for the conjecture's consequence.
events.remains: As in frecon-rank3-2016; the generalisation concerns sad groups, which are not the same as simple groups of the conjecture's kind.

events.what_happened: Adrien Deloro and Joshua Wiscons, 'Simple groups of Morley rank 5 are bad' (arXiv:1707.02057, v1 7 Jul 2017; no journal reference on the page). Per the arXiv abstract page as summarised: using the geometry of involutions in N°∘-groups of finite Morley rank (the page's notation), every simple group of Morley rank 5 is a bad group (every proper definable connected subgroup is nilpotent of rank at most 2); the result is used to catalogue the nonsoluble connected groups of Morley rank 5.
events.revisions: Single version (v1).
events.delivers: Rank-5 reduction: a simple group of finite Morley rank 5 would be a bad group. No simple algebraic group has dimension 5 (my inference from the list of simple algebraic groups), so any simple group of Morley rank 5 would be a counterexample to the finite Morley rank form. The result therefore reduces the rank-5 case to excluding bad groups of rank 5; it does not show that they do not exist.
events.remains: Whether any bad simple group of Morley rank 5 exists; the rank-5 case of the conjecture is equivalent to that question under the reduction.
events.direction: Narrows the rank-5 case to bad groups; neutral on existence.

events.what_happened: Tim Clausen and Katrin Tent, 'On the geometry of sharply 2-transitive groups' (arXiv:2002.05187, posted 12 Feb 2020). Per the arXiv abstract page as summarised from quoted segments: the geometry associated with certain non-split sharply 2-transitive groups contains no proper projective plane; for sharply 2-transitive groups of finite Morley rank, known rank inequalities are improved, and a sharply 2-transitive group of Morley rank 6 must be of the form K-semidirect-K* for an algebraically closed field K.
events.revisions: Single version (v1); no journal reference on the page.
events.delivers: Restricts sharply 2-transitive groups of finite Morley rank of Morley rank 6 to the split form K-semidirect-K*. Whether this touches the simple-group statement depends on whether such groups are simple: K-semidirect-K* is not simple, and I did not establish that any candidate sharply 2-transitive counterexample must be simple. The 2026 survey treats these groups as candidate sources of counterexamples (see tent-survey-2026). Read as a restriction of the simple-group statement, it is void; read as elimination of one candidate family, it is a partial result on the programme.
events.remains: Sharply 2-transitive groups of finite Morley rank at other ranks; non-split ones of other ranks; whether any sharply 2-transitive counterexample is simple.
events.direction: Eliminates one candidate family (rank-6 sharply 2-transitive groups, to the split form); its direction for the simple-group statement is unresolved.

summary: The conjecture as the literature states it is the finite Morley rank form (every simple group of finite Morley rank is algebraic); the bullet's ℵ0-stable form is broader and the literature does not close that gap. The status is open. Tent's ICM 2026 survey (arXiv 2606.18207, 16 Jun 2026) reports it confirmed for Morley rank at most 3 and wide open otherwise, and Cherlin's 2024 odd-type paper (Model Theory, published 19 Jul 2024) calls it unsettled and says one leans towards expecting counterexamples. The landmarks all predate the window: rank 3 (Frecon, arXiv 11 Jul 2016, JAMS 2018), a rank-5 reduction to bad groups (Deloro-Wiscons, 7 Jul 2017), odd-type reductions to Prufer 2-rank at most two and to minimal-counterexample shapes (Borovik-Burdges-Nesin, Borovik-Burdges, Burdges, all posted 27 Nov 2007; Burdges-Cherlin, 25 Jan 2008), degenerate type excluded (Borovik-Burdges-Cherlin, 27 Nov 2007), mixed type for tame K*-groups (Cherlin, dated only to 1996), and even type (Altinel-Borovik-Cherlin, dated to 1999 by a secondary source and consolidated in their 2008 monograph). The in-window items are neighbours (Berkman-Borovik 2024, Altinel-Wiscons 2024, Kowalski 2026, Karhumaki-Ramsey 2026, all on other conjectures) or a programme paper I could not read (Berkman-Borovik, Şiş Kebap, 2 Aug 2026). Close calls, both readings given: (1) Scope. Read literally, the bullet is false at finite simple groups, since their theories are ℵ0-stable and they are not algebraic; the Wikipedia 'Stable group' article says 'infinite (ω-stable) simple groups', so I have treated 'infinite' as implied. Even the finite Morley rank core is open, so no in-window result can settle the bullet. (2) Clausen-Tent (2020) gives the split form K-semidirect-K* for rank-6 sharply 2-transitive groups. It restricts a candidate family, but K-semidirect-K* is not simple, so it does not restrict the simple-group statement unless the candidates are simple, which I did not establish. (3) Deloro-Wiscons (2017) shows that a simple group of Morley rank 5 would be bad, so the rank-5 case reduces to excluding bad groups; it does not settle that case. (4) The Frecon 2016 preprint and the Poizat-Wagner comment (Sep 2016) agree on rank 3, and I found no error claimed against Frecon. (5) The Kowalski abstract page does not mention the conjecture, but a search excerpt says it notes Frecon's rank-3 result; I did not reconcile this. AI involvement: I found no AI system named in any source about this problem. My AI-targeted searches (the conjecture's name with GPT, Claude, LLM, AlphaProof, AlphaEvolve, Aristotle, Lean and the 2026 AI-mathematics announcements, plus the Borovik and Cherlin names) turned up nothing connecting AI to it. The 2026 AI-mathematics activity I found concerns other problems: OpenAI's Astra results of 1 Aug 2026 (including a non-sofic group), and the AI-assisted Kourovka-notebook paper arXiv 2608.29219, whose eight problems I did not check for finite Morley rank content. The none_found flags for the Tent survey and the Şiş Kebap paper rest on abstracts and excerpts only, because their bodies and acknowledgements were unreadable in my tools; that caveat applies to every none_found flag set after 2024.
competing_reading: Read the in-window programme papers as having moved the problem. Berkman-Borovik's Şiş Kebap paper (Aug 2026) is prepared for the Hrushovski programme of classifying infinite simple groups of finite Morley rank, which is the conjecture's home; if its body contains an identification of simple groups, or an odd-type case, the 'nothing happened' outcome is wrong. Read Clausen-Tent (2020) as eliminating a candidate counterexample family rather than as irrelevant; the 2026 survey treats it that way. Conversely, the strongest case for 'nothing happened' is that Tent's June 2026 survey, written after all these papers, lists the status and no in-window result closes a case, and that Cherlin's 2024 paper calls the odd-type problem unfinished.
what_would_settle_it: The full text of arXiv 2608.01161 (theorem statement, whether it identifies simple groups, and its acknowledgements); the full text of arXiv 2606.18207 (its status section, any new claims, and its references); the body of Cherlin's 2024 paper, especially its odd-type sections and any theorem it proves; the status of the 2022 Burdges-Cherlin L* drafts; a zbMATH or MathSciNet search for 2024-2026 papers on simple groups of finite Morley rank (zbMATH returned HTTP 403 to my tools); a check of whether any simple ω-stable group outside finite Morley rank is known (a search excerpt cites Corredor 2003 for an infinite simple non-ω-stable Frobenius group, which I did not open, and records Baudisch's non-simple nilpotent example).

judgement.why: Only two events settle restrictions of the statement: even type (Altinel-Borovik-Cherlin, monograph) and Morley rank 3 (Frecon, JAMS), both confirmed cases, both long before the snapshot; Poizat-Wagner reproves the rank-3 case. Degenerate-type, odd-type and rank-5 papers are reductions of a minimal counterexample, not settled classes, so none. Mixed type was scored variant because it carries tameness and K*-hypotheses absent from the statement. Sharply 2-transitive, Burnside, Borovik-Cherlin and automorphism papers concern different problems (variant). In-window, Cherlin 2024 and Tent 2026 are expository status reports calling the conjecture open (none), and the Sis Kebap paper's theorem was unreadable and its abstract claims only an identification tool for a programme, so none. No AI involvement anywhere.
judgement.doubts: The Sis Kebap paper (arXiv 2608.01161) was scored none on its abstract alone; if its body identifies simple groups in some class it could be a case. The literal statement omits 'infinite' and fails at finite simple groups; read as intended. Even-type date (1999) is secondary. AI none_found for post-2024 papers rests on abstracts only.
